query: I received a bill for $2,400 from my visit last month and my insurance was supposed to cover it. How do I dispute this?
response:
I’m sorry for the stress this is causing. Let’s get it reviewed. Here’s how to dispute or appeal a bill with us:

1) Gather documents
- Your Providence bill (account number and date of service)
- Your insurance Explanation of Benefits (EOB) for that visit
- Your insurance card
- Any prior authorizations or referral notes (if applicable)

2) Call us so we can review the claim
- Providence Patient Financial Services: 1-800-326-2873 (Mon–Fri, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. local time)
- Ask for a benefits/claim review and note that “insurance was expected to cover.”
- We’ll verify demographics, insurance details, coding, and whether a claim rejection/underpayment occurred.

3) Common issues we can resolve on the call
- Insurance info on file was outdated or keyed incorrectly
- Claim denied for coordination of benefits (COB) not updated
- Missing referral or prior authorization on record
- Out-of-network processing applied in error
- Services bundled or coded incorrectly

4) If a rebill or appeal is needed
- We can resubmit the claim to your insurer after corrections.
- If your insurer denied the claim, we’ll initiate a provider appeal when appropriate and provide any required medical records.
- You may need to file a member appeal with your insurer; we’ll give you the denial reason and any supporting documents. File member appeals within your plan’s deadline (often 30–60 days from the EOB).

5) Submit a formal billing dispute to Providence (optional/if you prefer in writing)
- Email: PFS@providence.org (include account number, date of service, brief description, and copies of EOBs)
- Mail: Providence Patient Financial Services, PO Box 3396, Portland, OR 97208-3396
- Please do not send full SSNs by email.

6) While it’s under review
- We can place a temporary hold on collections and stop late fees.
- Ask about an itemized bill; we’ll send it at no charge.
- If any balance is ultimately your responsibility, we can set up an interest-free payment plan or check financial assistance eligibility.

To get started now, please share:
- Your full name and date of birth
- Account number from the bill
- Date of service and location
- Your insurance plan name and member ID

If you prefer, I can flag your account and have a billing specialist call you. Let me know the best phone number and a good time to reach you.
ground_truth: Contact the hospital billing department, request an itemized bill, and file a formal dispute. Also contact your insurance to verify claims status and ask about the appeals process. Keep written records of all communications.

query: What is the earliest available appointment with a primary care physician accepting new patients?
response:
I can help you find the earliest available primary care appointment. To check real-time openings, I’ll need a few details:

- Your full name and date of birth (for our system)
- Whether you’re an existing Providence patient
- Your preferred clinic location (or zip code) and how far you can travel
- Any scheduling constraints (days/times)
- Do you prefer in-person or virtual?
- Insurance plan (so I can match you with a PCP accepting it)

If you’d prefer, you can also check and book immediately through:
- Providence Patient Portal: Log in and select “Schedule” > “Primary Care” to see live availability.
- Scheduling line: 555-0142 (Mon–Fri, 7:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m.)

Share the details above, and I’ll look up the first available appointment and offer a few options.
ground_truth: Availability varies by location and provider. Use the patient portal or call scheduling directly to see current openings. Typical wait times for new-patient primary care are 2-4 weeks.

query: As a new employee, how do I enroll in the employer health plan and what is the deadline?
response:
Welcome to Providence! Here’s how to enroll in the employer health plan:

How to enroll
- Look for your “New Hire Benefits Enrollment” email from HR (subject line: “Providence Benefits—Action Required”). It includes your Employee ID and a link to the Benefits Portal.
- Or, log into the Providence Employee Benefits Portal directly:
  - URL: benefits.providence.org (use your network login; first-time users will be prompted to set up MFA).
  - Navigate to: My Benefits > New Hire Enrollment.
- Review plan options (medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, and optional life/STD/LTD), add dependents, and select your coverage.
- Upload any required documentation for dependents (e.g., marriage license, birth certificates) before you submit.
- Complete your e-signature and print/save your confirmation page.

Deadline
- You must enroll within 30 days of your hire date (or your benefits-eligibility date stated in your offer letter). If you miss this window, you’ll need to wait until the next Open Enrollment or a qualifying life event to make changes.

Coverage effective date
- Coverage typically begins on the first of the month following your hire date, provided you enroll on time. Your confirmation page will show your exact effective date.

Need help?
- Benefits Service Center: 800-555-0199, Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. local time.
- Email: benefits@providence.org
- If you don’t see the portal email within two business days of your start date, check spam and then contact HR Shared Services at 855-PRV-HR4U.

If you share your hire date, I can confirm your enrollment deadline and expected coverage start date.
ground_truth: New employees typically have 30 days from their start date to enroll. Log into the HR benefits portal, select your plan, add dependents, and submit before the deadline. Contact HR Benefits for personalized help.

query: What are the visiting hours for the cardiac ICU?
response:
Providence Hospital Cardiac ICU visiting hours are 10:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. daily.

A few reminders:
- Two visitors at a time at the bedside (exceptions may be made for end-of-life or special circumstances with charge nurse approval).
- Visitors must be age 12+; younger visitors require prior approval.
- Please use hand hygiene before and after visiting and do not visit if you’re ill.
- Quiet hours are observed to support patient rest; staff may limit visit length during procedures or clinical care.

If you have a specific patient you’re visiting, you can call the Cardiac ICU desk at 555-0148 before coming to confirm current restrictions or any temporary changes.
ground_truth: Cardiac ICU visiting hours are typically more restricted than general wards, often limited to specific windows (e.g., 10am-8pm) with 2 visitors at a time. Call the unit directly for current policies since they change.

query: How do I request copies of my medical records for a second opinion?
response:
We’re happy to help. You can request your medical records from Providence Hospital in a few ways:

1) Online (fastest):
- Log in to the Providence Patient Portal.
- Go to Medical Records or Document Requests.
- Select the date range and document types (e.g., visit notes, imaging reports, labs).
- Indicate if you want them sent directly to another provider (enter their fax/email) or to you.

2) By form/email or mail:
- Complete the “Authorization to Release Medical Information” form.
- Include: your full name, DOB, phone, dates of service, specific records requested, delivery method (portal, mail, fax, secure email), and where to send.
- Attach a copy of a photo ID.
- Submit to Health Information Management (HIM/Medical Records):
  • Email: him@providencehospital.org (secure)
  • Fax: 555-012-3344
  • Mail: Providence Hospital – HIM Dept, 123 Wellness Ave, Suite 200, Providence, ST 00000

3) In person:
- Visit the HIM office (Main Hospital, 2nd Floor). Bring a photo ID. Hours: Mon–Fri, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

Fees and timing:
- Standard records are usually free when sent to another healthcare provider for treatment.
- Copies for personal use may have a nominal fee per page per state law; we’ll notify you before charging.
- Processing time: 3–7 business days. Imaging CDs/USBs may take up to 10 business days.

For imaging (X‑ray/CT/MRI):
- You can request images plus the radiology report on CD or via a secure download link. If sending to another provider, provide their contact details.

Authorization notes:
- If your request includes mental health, substance use, HIV/STD, or reproductive health records, please initial those specific sections on the form.
- For minors or those with a legal representative, include guardianship or POA documentation.

Need help completing the request?
- Call Medical Records at 555-012-2211 (Mon–Fri, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.), or reply here and I can send you the release form and portal link. If you provide the destination clinic’s info, we can send it directly for your second opinion.
ground_truth: Submit a signed medical records release form to the Health Information Management (HIM) department. You can do this online via the patient portal or in person. Records are typically provided within 30 days, though urgent requests can be expedited.

query: How much is parking at the main hospital campus?
response:
Parking at the Providence main hospital campus is free for patients and visitors. 

- Patient/visitor garages and surface lots are open 24/7.
- Please keep your parking ticket handy if a gate arm is in use; attendants can assist if needed.
- Accessible parking and short-term drop-off zones are available near main entrances.

If you’re coming for an appointment and need the best garage/lot for your clinic, tell me which department or building you’re visiting and I’ll guide you to the closest parking.
ground_truth: Visitor parking is typically $5-10 per day with discounted rates for extended stays. Validated parking is available for some clinic visits. Check the hospital website or information desk for current rates.

query: Do you accept Aetna PPO? I want to confirm before scheduling a procedure.
response:
Yes, Providence Hospital is in-network for most Aetna PPO plans. Coverage can vary by specific plan and service, so we recommend:

- Verify your plan: Call the number on your Aetna ID card or check your Aetna member portal to confirm Providence Hospital and your provider are in-network for your procedure.
- Share your details: If you’d like, I can check our system. Please provide your full name, date of birth, the Aetna plan name (as shown on your card), and the procedure you’re scheduling.
- Pre-authorization: Many procedures require prior authorization from Aetna. Our scheduling team can help submit the request once you book.

Would you like me to connect you with our scheduling and insurance verification team?
ground_truth: The hospital accepts most major insurance plans including Aetna PPO, but coverage depends on your specific plan. Call patient financial services or the insurance verification line with your policy details for confirmation.

query: I can't log into the patient portal - it says my password is incorrect but I just reset it.
response:
I’m sorry for the trouble. Let’s get you back in.

Quick checks:
- Make sure you’re using your MyChart/Patient Portal username (not your email unless you’ve set email as username).
- Confirm you’re on the Providence patient portal sign-in page and not another system.
- Try copying/pasting the temporary password carefully if you used one—avoid extra spaces.
- Clear your browser cache or try a different browser/device.
- If you use a password manager, update the saved password and try again.

Reset steps (if needed):
1) Go to our Patient Portal login page and select “Forgot Password.”
2) Enter your username and date of birth.
3) Use the password reset link sent to your email or the code sent by text (check spam/junk).
4) Create a new password (at least 8 characters, with a number and special character). Wait 1–2 minutes, then try logging in again.

Account lockouts:
- After several failed attempts, the account may lock for 15 minutes. If you see a lockout message, wait and try again, or request an unlock.

Two-step verification:
- If you have 2-step verification, be sure you’re completing the code step. If codes aren’t coming through, choose “Use a different method.”

If it still won’t work:
- I can verify your account and send a secure password reset/unlock link.
  • Please provide your full name, date of birth, and the email or mobile number on file (last 4 digits for security).
- Or contact the Patient Portal Support Line: 1-888-274-7849 (daily, 6am–6pm PT).

Let me know what error message you’re seeing (exact wording), and what you’ve tried so far, and I’ll guide you step-by-step.
ground_truth: Try clearing your browser cache, use the 'Forgot Password' flow again, and ensure your email is verified. If it still fails, call the patient portal support line; they can reset your account.

query: I'm interested in volunteering at the hospital. What opportunities are available?
response:
We’re excited you’re interested in volunteering at Providence Hospital! Our Volunteer Services program typically offers opportunities in the following areas based on availability:

- Patient & Family Support: Greeting visitors, wayfinding, concierge desks, family waiting rooms.
- Unit Support: Non-clinical assistance on patient units (restocking supplies, errands, comfort rounds).
- Outpatient & Clinic Support: Check-in assistance, escorts, phone support.
- Gift Shop & Hospitality: Gift shop sales, comfort cart, waiting room host.
- Therapy & Rehab Support: Assisting staff with activities (non-clinical).
- Administrative/Clerical: Data entry, filing, mailings for various departments.
- Special Events & Fundraising: Foundation events, drives, and community outreach.
- Pet Therapy (certified teams): For handlers with qualifying therapy-animal certification.
- Student/Teen Programs (seasonal): Limited placements for high school/college students.

Basic requirements:
- Minimum age: typically 16 for most roles (18+ for some areas).
- Application, interview, and background check.
- Health clearance: immunizations (e.g., TB screening, flu/COVID per season).
- Orientation and role-specific training.
- Commitment: commonly 3–4 hours per week for 3–6 months.

How to apply:
- Complete the Volunteer Application form and availability checklist.
- Provide proof of immunizations and ID for background screening.
- Attend orientation (virtual or on-site).
- Schedule your first shift with Volunteer Services.

If you’d like, I can:
- Email you the current openings and application link.
- Tell you the next orientation date.
- Answer questions about age requirements, schedule, or placement preferences.

Please share your email address and any preferences (days/times, areas of interest, age/student status), and I’ll get you started. You can also reach Volunteer Services directly at 555-0142 or volunteer@providencehospital.org (Mon–Fri, 9am–4pm).
ground_truth: Volunteer opportunities typically include patient greeting, gift shop, administrative support, and comfort-care programs. Visit the volunteer services page on the hospital website or contact the Volunteer Office to start an application.

query: What are the hours for the main cafeteria and does it accommodate gluten-free diets?
response:
Here are the standard hours and dietary options for the Providence Hospital main cafeteria:

Hours (Main Cafeteria)
- Monday–Friday: 6:30 AM–7:00 PM
  - Breakfast: 6:30–10:00 AM
  - Lunch: 11:00 AM–2:00 PM
  - Dinner/Grill & Grab‑and‑Go: 4:30–7:00 PM
- Weekends/Holidays: 7:00 AM–2:00 PM (limited menu and grab‑and‑go items)

Gluten‑free accommodations
- Yes, we offer gluten‑free options daily, including salads, soups (labeled), grilled proteins, vegetables, and packaged grab‑and‑go items. Most stations label common allergens, including gluten.
- If you have celiac disease or severe gluten sensitivity, please inform the cashier or a supervisor so they can assist with ingredient checks and cross‑contact precautions.

Note: Hours and offerings can vary slightly by location or on holidays. If you’d like, tell me which Providence campus you’re visiting and the date, and I can confirm the exact schedule and options for that day.
ground_truth: The main cafeteria is typically open 6:30am-8pm with gluten-free options available at most stations. Dedicated gluten-free preparation areas help prevent cross-contamination. Contact food services for specific dietary needs.
